title: Selecting the Best Few with Human Evaluators: Adaptively Combining Ratings and Pairwise Comparisons
abstract: arXiv:2610.26380v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: This paper considers a decision-maker tasked with identifying the $k$ best items from a large pool of candidates, such as job applicants, LLMs, award nominees, or new product ideas. The decision-maker learns about the items' quality by soliciting human evaluations. Each evaluation can be costly, so the decision-maker aims to use the limited evaluation budget efficiently by allocating evaluations adaptively. A key consideration is the form of evaluation to solicit, which should be something evaluators are comfortable providing. Two popular forms are ratings and pairwise comparisons, and we allow for both, as they may be especially useful in combination given the limited budget. Ratings can be used early on to get a coarse picture of which items are good and which are not. translated_title: 借助人工评估者选出最优少数：自适应地结合评分与两两比较
translated_abstract: 本文研究这样一个决策者问题：需要从大量候选者（如求职者、大语言模型、奖项提名人或新产品创意）中识别出最优的 $k$ 个项目。决策者通过征集人工评估来了解各项目的质量。由于每次评估都可能成本高昂，决策者希望通过自适应地分配评估来高效利用有限的评估预算。一个关键考虑因素是所征集的评估形式，这种形式应当是评估者乐于提供的。两种流行的形式是评分和两两比较，我们对两者都加以考虑，因为在预算有限的情况下，二者的结合可能尤其有用。评分可以在早期使用，以大致了解哪些项目好、哪些项目不好。随着这一图景逐渐成形，两两比较可以细化优秀项目之间的排序，从而聚焦于最终的 top-$k$ 选择。为了解决这一分配问题，
tldr: 本文提出一种自适应评估分配方法，先利用人工评分对候选项目进行粗筛，再借助两两比较精化优秀项目的排序，从而在有限评估预算下高效地从大量候选中选出最优的 $k$ 个项目。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an adaptive evaluation allocation approach that first uses human ratings to coarsely screen candidates and then employs pairwise comparisons to refine the ranking of top items, efficiently identifying the top-k selections under a limited evaluation budget.
